lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 the comparison target has a name, a date, and a public sibling. (1) Upstream vLLM officially ships 'Marlin for Turing (sm75)': PR #29901 '[Kernel][Quantization][MoE] add marlin kernel support for turing (sm75)' by Jinzhen Lin (Ant Group), merged 2025-12-16 (co-authored/reviewed by Michael Goin), first released in v0.14.0 (tag 2026-01-16, release notes 2026-01-20 listing 'Marlin for Turing (sm75)' under Quantization); follow-ups #31000 and #31008 (2025-12-19) lowered the compressed-tensors Marlin gates from 8.0 to 7.5. The port's mechanics are verified at the fork pin (79378fe6e8, 2026-08-27): csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/marlin/marlin.cuh compiles every cp_async* helper below __CUDA_ARCH__ 800 into synchronous LDG->STS pointer copies with no-op commit/wait fences; marlin_mma.h adds six __CUDA_ARCH__==750 blocks (FP16 m16n8k16 split into two m16n8k8 issues, m16n8k8, INT8 m8n8k16); generate_kernels.py emits a dedicated sm75 config table with config_sm75['stages']=2 versus 4 on Ampere; CMakeLists.txt carries dedicated MARLIN_SM75_ARCHS / MARLIN_MOE_SM75_ARCHS (7.5) build blocks. This is exactly the pipelining substitution: original Marlin (IST-DASLab/marlin; Frantar et al., arXiv:2408.11743, PPoPP'25) requires compute capability >= 8.0 and its multi-stage cp.async global->shared pipeline overlapping tensor-core compute is the core Ampere mechanism behind the paper's near-ideal ~4x speedups up to batch 16-32. (2) The PR author's own 2080 Ti numbers (dense GPTQ): vs torch-fp16 channelwise n2048/k4096 m=1: ~0.032 ms -> ~0.0115 ms w4a16 (~2.8x) and ~0.0106 ms w4a8-int8; vs GPTQ exllama v2 group-128 4096x4096 m=1: ~0.021 vs ~0.026 ms and 8192x2048 m=8: ~0.063 vs ~0.083 ms; Marlin trails the dequant+cuBLAS path at large batch (the original GPTQ kernel switches to cuBLAS above m=8). The author also states that on Turing (and Ada) MMA throughput halves with an FP32 accumulator versus FP16, motivating the port's Turing-only use_fp16_accum - this conflicts with this host's TU102 microbench (f32-acc equals f16-acc at ~101 TFLOP/s on the m16n8k8 shape) and is unverified here; plausibly a full-kernel register-pressure/occupancy effect rather than pipe throughput [uncertain]. (3) Formats on sm75 after #29901: GPTQ/AWQ W4A16, W4A8-INT8 activations, FP8-weights W8A16 (fp8.py get_min_capability lowered 80->75 in the same PR; compressed_tensors W8A16-FP8 scheme get_min_capability 75 routing to MarlinFP8; docs.vllm.ai: 'Turing/Ampere GPUs are supported for W8A16 (weight-only FP8) utilizing Marlin kernels' and 'FP8 models will run on compute capability >= 7.5 (Turing) as weight-only W8A16, utilizing FP8 Marlin'), and NVFP4A16; MXFP4 was excluded because it needs BF16 activations, which Turing lacks. (4) Post-v0.14 evolution through the pin: #33076 (2026-01-27) compressed-tensors nvfp4/fp8 weights + modelopt nvfp4 on Turing; #43731 (2026-05-27) TritonW4A16LinearKernel as CUDA fallback for non-Marlin-aligned W4A16 shapes; #45176 (2026-06-11) torch stable-ABI migration moving the kernels to csrc/libtorch_stable/; #45295/#45703 (2026-06-12/23) Marlin thread-tile padding for dense then MoE; #45375 (2026-06-22) modelopt_mixed on Turing; #49376 (2026-07-26) documentation of NVFP4 GEMM selection with Marlin weight-only fallback; #52966 (2026-08-19) compressed-tensors block-FP8 with Marlin. None of these reworks the sm75 pipeline itself: the two-stage cp.async substitution is unchanged since Dec 2025, so the incumbent the host must beat is still current upstream. (5) The sibling benchmark target: weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive (created 2026-06-02, 815 stars / 123 forks, default branch vllm-2080ti-definitive-0.1.x, last push 2026-09-04, releases v0.1.16 2026-08-20, v0.1.17 2026-08-24, v0.2.1-pre3 2026-08-27; base vLLM 0.21.0 with CUDA 12.8, torch 2.11.0+cu128, driver 590.48.01) - a dual 22GB RTX 2080 Ti + NVLink TP=2 single-user serving fork carrying Marlin routes for FP8, GPTQ/AWQ INT4, NVFP4, and QAT, FlashInfer attention plus a FlashQLA-SM70-SM75 adaptation, TurboQuant K8V4 KV compression, INT8 KV, MTP speculative decoding, and a CUDAGraph-first runtime. Engine-level measurements published in its README: Qwen3.6-27B FP8 at 100+ tok/s single-request decode; 4096/128 GPTQ-INT4 MTP3 route ~91 tok/s on an i3-9100T host (~56 on dual Xeon X5675); 256K text-only and 178K fast/MTP3 context validated on a 35B MoE; hardware argument: dual 2080 Ti ~ 1.43x dense FP16 tensor throughput and 1.83x VRAM of a 3090 Ti at roughly half the used price. No GEMM TFLOP/s microbenchmarks are published in that repo, so the comparison must be run, not read. (6) Community signal: the r/LocalLLaMA v0.14.0 release thread calls Marlin-for-Turing the release's major upgrade ('we can once again use T4/T10/2080Ti or similar GPUs for 32B-AWQ models', with a small user benchmark); a post-merge T4 report in #29901 (mokieli, Dec 18 2025) shows Qwen3-Next-80B AWQ loading via the Marlin MoE method but failing later on the separate BF16-on-Turing torch.compile limitation; a vLLM forum thread ('Why I feel cuda-kernel marlin run not fast') documents Marlin efficiency dropping to ~60% or less at very large batch sizes [uncertain URL]; the AI-Muninn blog 'Why Isn't Your 4-Bit Quant Faster on a 2080 Ti?' (2026) argues Turing has no mixed-width MMA (s4xf16 columns empty in an nm -D dump 'on every architecture'), walks back its own earlier sm_80-only claim after vLLM v0.27.1-era docs showed Marlin sm75 support since ~v0.14, characterizes Marlin on 2080 Ti as 'a dequant kernel, just a well-optimized one', and cites the TurboMind paper (arXiv:2508.15601) for the load-INT4 -> I2F -> dequant-to-fp16 -> fp16-GEMM sequence all W4A16 kernels share on this silicon.
lacuna.sm75_viability: What runs on Turing-class hardware today, with numbers. (1) Upstream dense + MoE Marlin for GPTQ/AWQ W4A16 (+W4A8-INT8 activations), FP8-weights W8A16, and NVFP4A16 ships in every vLLM release from v0.14.0 (Jan 2026) through the current v0.28-era tip; verified at the fork pin building via the dedicated 7.5 arch blocks and running on this host's Quadro RTX 6000 at locked 1455 MHz at 51-57 TFLOP/s at M512 across the model shapes (N4096/K4096, N11008/K4096, N4096/K11008), float64-checked, weight-bound near 1 TFLOP/s (0.60) at M1 in the N=K=4096 table; T4 community runs confirm the MoE path loads (with the separate BF16 torch.compile caveat for hybrid-architecture models). (2) The fork's own kernels are correct and already win every decode regime: opt1 (fp16-staged) and opt2 (register-dequant) pass the float64 oracle and post 0.16/1.26/4.79 TFLOP/s at M=1/8/32 versus the incumbent's 0.60/4.86/13.98 - it is the large-M/prefill regime (M>=128: 17.5-23.5 vs 35.1-51.4) where the acceptance clause fails, worst case 2.2x at M512. (3) Full sm75 serving is proven by the weicj fork on dual 2080 Ti (FP8/INT4/NVFP4/QAT Marlin routes, >100 tok/s decode on a 27B FP8 model), so engine-level targets on the 2x RTX 6000 rig are realistic. Capability floors and their real blockers, all measured on this host: no cp.async below sm80 - the incumbent's synchronous LDG->STS substitution with a forced stages=2 config is precisely the pipelining deficit the remaining work attacks, and deeper stages cost shared memory against the occupancy red-line (one resident block caps the tensor pipes at 43.8 TFLOP/s; two reach the 101.7 ceiling - a legality gate, not a knob, for any deep-pipe candidate); no sanctioned INT4 MMA (ptxas rejects .s4 for mma m8n8k16 on sm75, so register dequant is permanent; the AI-Muninn nm -D observation that same-width s4 SASS ops exist is not actionable through the sanctioned PTX interface and is an unverified external claim [uncertain]); the k8 wall (m16n8k16 f32-acc requires sm80 - every k16 tile is two k8 issues, inherited operand-staging cost); no BF16 (MXFP4 excluded); FP16 tensor ceiling 101.7 TFLOP/s at 1455 MHz; DRAM 535 GB/s; W4A16 crossover M*~47, below which weight bytes (not tensor-pipe efficiency) are the lever. The contention table prices dequant ALU against HMMA (16 ALU per 4 HMMAs drops the stream to ~24 percent), which is why the repack interlace / skip_flop two-lop3 economy and register-resident fragments are the named path from 23-25 toward and past 51-57. Fallback semantics: since #43731 (2026-05-27), W4A16 shapes not Marlin-aligned route to TritonW4A16LinearKernel on CUDA - on sm75 Triton lowers to mma.884/FMA codegen with known floors, so the fork's N%128 requirement (BN=128 configs) and the upstream thread-tile-padding rules (#45295/#45703) are the silent-fallback surface to keep loud; NVFP4 on non-Blackwell lands on Marlin weight-only per the #49376-documented selection; FP8 checkpoints run as W8A16 Marlin on cc>=7.5 per the official FP8 docs. The attention-backend candidate matrix does not gate this dense-GEMM item; it gates only the engine-level comparison runs against the weicj stack.
lacuna.upstream_base: Dated ledger for the sm75 Marlin surface. 2024: Marlin imported into vLLM from IST-DASLab (sm80+ only; upstream README requires compute capability >= 8.0). 2024-08/2025-02: Marlin paper (arXiv:2408.11743; PPoPP'25, DOI 10.1145/3710848.3710871) - multi-stage cp.async pipeline, LOP3 in-register dequant, ~4x to batch 16-32. 2025-12-16: PR #29901 merged - sm75 Marlin dense+MoE (marlin.cuh cp.async->synchronous-copy substitution below sm80 with no-op fences; marlin_mma.h six sm750 MMA atoms incl. the k16-as-2xk8 split; generate_kernels.py sm75 config table with stages=2; CMake MARLIN_SM75_ARCHS; fp8.py min capability 80->75). 2025-12-19: PRs #31000 (MarlinLinearKernel.get_min_capability 8.0->7.5, compressed-tensors) and #31008 (marlin_utils gate, same day) [uncertain: #31008 merge timestamp not independently confirmed, gh-adjacent PR page states merged same day as #31000]. 2026-01-16 tag / 2026-01-20 release: v0.14.0 - first release carrying 'Marlin for Turing (sm75) (#29901, #31000)'. 2026-01-27: #33076 compressed-tensors nvfp4/fp8 weights + modelopt nvfp4 on Turing. 2026-05-14: v0.21.0 tag (the weicj fork's base). 2026-05-27: #43731 Triton W4A16 CUDA fallback for non-Marlin-aligned shapes. 2026-06-11: #45176 torch stable-ABI migration (kernels moved to csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/marlin/ - the fork's last upstream touch of this file family). 2026-06-12: #45295 thread-tile padding, dense Marlin paths. 2026-06-22: #45375 modelopt_mixed on Turing. 2026-06-23: #45703 tile padding extended to MoE (WNA16+FP8/MXFP8). 2026-07-26: #49376 docs - NVFP4 GEMM kernel selection and Marlin weight-only fallback. 2026-08-19: #52966 compressed-tensors block-FP8 with Marlin. 2026-08-27: fork pin 79378fe6e8 (ancestor of #53666) contains all of the above; no vLLM release from v0.14.0 through the v0.28-era tip dropped or degraded sm75 Marlin, and the sm75 pipeline mechanics (stages=2, sync-copy substitution, fp16-accum option) are untouched since #29901. Consequence for rebasing: the pin is the last-good base, no sm75-specific churn forces a rebase, and the only structural move to absorb on the next rebase is the stable-ABI file relocation (#45176), already absorbed in the fork tree.

effort_value.effort_estimate: A full campaign continuation, not an adapter or a single ladder run. Named remaining work, in decreasing certainty of effect: (1) repack-interleave consumption - make the kernel eat the real Marlin repacked weight layout (or the regdeq2 staging-side nibble interleave already implemented and oracle-clean at 2x scale smem) so the skip_flop two-lop3 dequant stream applies, deleting the byte_perm and the staging-multiply that the pipe kernel showed costs 13-14 vs 23-25 TFLOP/s; (2) deeper software pipeline - pipe3+ variants through propose.py's row interface over the register-resident-dequant kernel, respecting the occupancy legality gate (>=2 resident blocks) that deeper stages' shared-memory cost threatens; (3) split-K small-M refinement beyond the landed dispatch-table winner (regdeq_64_128_64_w4x2 nz=2) and the kshard2 fp32-partials cross-GPU path; (4) a one-session ncu decomposition of the incumbent at M512 pricing the 51-57 into pipeline-depth vs occupancy vs dequant-economy components, to size the recoverable margin against the 101.7 wall before spending ladder budget; (5) the new comparison benchmarks - reproduce PR #29901's own 2080 Ti table on this host, and port/benchmark the weicj stack engine-level on the 2x RTX 6000 rig. Rough size: 2-4 weeks of kernel-ladder sessions for items 1-4 plus 2-3 sessions for item 5; everything rides the existing 2x float64-oracle + SASS-gate + occupancy-legality + winner-gate machinery, so no new harness is needed.
effort_value.unlocks: Closes the last open acceptance clause of plan/0002 (demonstrated improvement in the targeted regimes with no unacceptable worst-case regression - currently a 2.2x regression at M512, 23.49 vs 51.38 TFLOP/s); roughly doubles the fork's W4A16 dense throughput ceiling toward the measured 101.7 TFLOP/s wall, which is prefill/encode throughput for GPTQ/AWQ models on the operator's 2x Quadro RTX 6000 serving rig; compounds the already-banked decode wins (the dispatch table feeds M<=8 decode batches from the same kernel family); establishes the externally defensible comparison the fork's reason-to-exist needs - beat upstream 'Marlin for Turing' (v0.14.0+) on its own sm75 silicon and match the weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive sibling's engine-level targets; and produces the machinery (repack-format consumption, deep-pipe configs, split-K epilogues) that the W8A8-INT8 track (203 TOPS, lever 2) and the W2A16 byte-reduction lane (plan/0005) reuse directly.
effort_value.dependency_order: Already landed (prerequisites, in order): reference backend and float64 oracle; kernel-search ladder with propose.py row interface and SASS/occupancy gates; dispatch-table winner gates (plan/0003/0004); regdeq2 swizzled staging (oracle-clean, awaiting its final ladder rung); kshard2 fp32 partials (oracle-clean, 1.68x at M64 over NVLink); the B-fragment layout resolution that validated opt2 register-dequant; TU102 characterization red-lines (occupancy legality, k8 wall, s4 absence). Must land next: (a) the repack-interlace contract resolution (consume the real Marlin repacked format or keep regdeq2's staging-side interleave) - prerequisite for the skip_flop-style dequant stream the deep pipeline overlaps; (b) pipe3+ variants - can start immediately in parallel on the existing staging format, the two tracks converging in a regdeq2+pipe3 combination row; (c) split-K small-M refinement - independent and parallelizable, already admissible through the dispatch table. External prerequisites: none for the kernel work (upstream #29901 is at the pin; all primitives are sm75-sanctioned PTX); the weicj comparison needs its repo cloned and its CUDA 12.8 / torch 2.11 stack reconciled with this host's CUDA 13.3 build (a configuration exercise, days not weeks); the rope sm_86 reference runs are done and attested and do not gate. Not gating but adjacent: the MoE integration acceptance item shares the same kernels and follows the dense close.
effort_value.risk_notes: Numerics: (1) the FP16-vs-FP32 accumulator decision - the upstream port uses fp16 accumulation on Turing citing halved MMA throughput, which this host's m16n8k8 microbench contradicts (equal at ~101 TFLOP/s); if fp16 accum is adopted for register footprint it must be separately oracle-gated at K=11008 where accumulation depth is worst, and the in-kernel A/B must be run before believing either claim [uncertain: the upstream author's halving claim is unverified on TU102]; (2) split-K changes accumulation order and already produced one fp16-partial oracle failure (kshard2) - the fp32-partial epilogue stays mandatory; (3) the repack-interleave path carries the 16x relative-scaling asymmetry finding (nibble pairs share a byte in the m16n8k8 B fragment) - the oracle case set must include asymmetric weights or a wrong interleave passes false-clean; (4) skip_flop folds a bias correction into the scales - group-boundary and zero-point-mode adversarial cases must remain in the oracle. Silent fallbacks: since #43731, non-Marlin-aligned W4A16 shapes silently route to Triton W4A16 (mma.884/FMA codegen on sm75) - the fork's dispatch must mark that route loudly or a perf regression masquerades as kernel slowness; opt2's N%128==0 restriction is the main alignment surface. CUDA-graph interaction: deeper pipelines add stages and barriers, and the split-K WS-zero replay-ordering defect (turing_lab/probes/cuda_graph_validation.md) must be re-verified per new admitted config. Upstream drift: bounded - the sm75 mechanics are untouched upstream since Dec 2025, the pin strategy absorbs the stable-ABI file move already, and the only semantic drift to watch on rebase is the tile-padding behavior change (#45295/#45703) in shape dispatch. Benchmark validity: PR #29901's 2080 Ti numbers and the weicj tok/s numbers come from different clocks/stacks (CUDA 12.8 vs 13.3) - cross-comparisons must be re-based onto this host's locked-clock protocol before any claim.
effort_value.determinism_class: Two mechanisms set the class. (1) The GEMM main loop is bitwise deterministic per configuration: fixed tile traversal, fixed k-fragment order, no atomics in the non-split path - incumbent and fork kernels alike reproduce bit-exactly run-to-run at fixed shape/config, so the float64-oracle gate is an exact-diff under fp16 tolerance and 2x deterministic passes are meaningful. (2) Split-K / global reduction: the incumbent offers both a locks-based fixed-order reduce (bitwise: slices reduce in slice-index order under barrier_acquire on the caller-zeroed workspace) and use_atomic_add (atomicAdd ordering varies run-to-run - statistical class); the fork's kshard2 writes fp32 partials with a deterministic fixed-order reduce, and the current dispatch-table small-M winner (regdeq_64_128_64_w4x2 nz=2) inherits whichever epilogue it ships, so the winner-gate transcript must record which class each admitted row is. Run-to-run variance sources: atomic scheduling order only (timing methodology already neutralizes it via median-of-N at locked clocks; numerics methodology via the 2x oracle passes). Restart-to-restart: workspace/lock zero state - a fresh process re-zeros the workspace (caller contract), and a replayed CUDA graph must express the zeroing (the recorded replay defect: WS-zero ordering under capture); deeper pipeline stages add barriers but no new ordering nondeterminism. What the float64-oracle + median-of-N discipline needs to hold here: split-K candidates gated on the fixed-order epilogue (or their atomic-path variance bounded by the adversarial oracle set), any fp16-accumulator variant gated at K=11008, and the repack-interleave oracle cases carrying asymmetric weights so a layout error cannot pass clean.

decision.priority_signal: For doing this next: the plan/0002 acceptance contract is explicitly open and this is now the only failing regime (M>=128; worst case 2.2x at M512) while every decode regime is already won (0.16-4.79 vs 0.60-13.98 at M 1-32); the gap decomposition is measured on this host, not speculative - the contention table prices dequant ALU against HMMA, the occupancy red-line and the 101.7 ceiling bound the recoverable margin at ~2x past the incumbent; the upstream comparison target now has a name and a date (Marlin for Turing, v0.14.0, Jan 2026) plus an active public sibling (weicj fork, 815 stars, pushed 2026-09-04), so 'beat upstream sm75 Marlin on its own silicon' is a defensible, publishable result with a real window; and the machinery (regdeq2, kshard2-fp32, propose.py gates) is already landed, so the marginal cost is ladder time, not infrastructure. Against: upstream itself is not racing (the sm75 two-stage substitution is untouched for nine months - no closing window from that side); the operator's serving sweet spot is decode, which is memory-bound below the M*~47 crossover and already won, so the remaining acceptance item buys prefill throughput, which the W2A16 byte-reduction lane or speculative-decoding multipliers could buy more cheaply; and the effort is weeks against days for engine-level lanes. Window-closing risk: low-medium - nothing upstream threatens the result, but the weicj 0.2.x line and upstream MoE work keep moving the engine-level comparison baseline, and every month of pin age adds rebase surface. Net: high value, moderate urgency - schedule next unless the operator's near-term target is strictly decode-only latency.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0, oracle-first, no new kernels, three cheap steps. (1) One-session ncu decomposition of the incumbent sm75 Marlin at M512/N=K=4096 on locked clocks: HMMA pipe utilization, achieved occupancy and resident blocks, shared-memory/barrier stall breakdown, and the sm75 config row actually dispatched (stages=2, threads, tile) - this prices the 51-57 TFLOP/s into pipeline-depth vs occupancy vs dequant-economy components and sizes the recoverable margin against the 101.7 ceiling before any ladder spend; run the same counters on opt2 (23-25) for the differential. (2) Reproduce PR #29901's own benchmark table on this host (torch-fp16 vs exllama-v2 vs Marlin at the PR's shapes, m=1..64) under the locked-clock protocol - this anchors cross-comparability with the upstream author's 2080 Ti numbers and the weicj stack before any fork-vs-upstream claim is made. (3) Push the already-implemented regdeq2 row plus one pipe3 variant through the standing gates (2x float64 oracle with asymmetric-weight and K=11008 cases, SASS gate, occupancy legality >=2 resident blocks) and run the existing dispatch harness once - if regdeq2+pipe3 closes even half the M512 gap in harness-relative terms, the campaign is confirmed and ordered; if it moves nothing, step (1)'s decomposition redirects the work (occupancy vs dequant economy) before more ladder budget burns. Timing only after oracles pass, per the standing rules; absolute small-M claims still via marlin_bench-style runs, not the selection harness.
